question: What is the difference between a Secret and a ConfigMap in Kubernetes, and what does each store?

ground_truth.answer: Both Secret and ConfigMap store key-value data that Pods can consume as environment variables or mounted files. The distinction is in the intended use and encoding of the data. ConfigMap stores non-sensitive configuration values in plain text. Secret stores sensitive data — passwords, tokens, keys — with values encoded in base64 in the API representation. The type field on Secret is a string that categorizes the Secret; its value is not enforced or enumerated by the schema definition itself but is used by Kubernetes components and admission controllers to select the appropriate handling. Both resources use similar injection mechanisms (envFrom, volume mounts) via the same Container fields.
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.Secret: stores sensitive data (passwords, tokens, keys); values are base64-encoded in the API; type field categorizes the Secret
io.k8s.api.core.v1.ConfigMap: stores non-sensitive configuration data as plain-text key-value pairs
